Input grid I. mostcolor x0 = most common color (background likely 0). x1 = asobject(I): all cells as (color,(i,j)). x2 = matcher(first, x0): function color==background. x3 = flip => color != background. x4 = sfilter(x1,x3): object of non-background cells (all colored pixels), each as (value,index). x5 = apply(initset,x4): singleton objects for each colored cell.

x6 = product(x5,x5): all ordered pairs of colored cells (singletons). x7=color first, x8=color last, x9 equality => same color. x10 = pairs of colored cells with same color.

x11 leftmost first, x12 leftmost last, x13 equality same column j. x14 uppermost first, x15 uppermost last, x16 same row i. x17 either x13 or x16: pairs in same column or same row.

x18 = pairs same color and (same row or same col). For each such pair, x19 color, x20 center first, x21 center last, x22 connect centers (line). x23 recolor color to connected indices. x37 = mapply x23 over x18: union of all lines between same-colored pairs that are in same row or column. x38 = paint(I, x37). This fills horizontal/vertical lines between same-colored cells. But note pairs include same cell? product includes (cell,cell); same color, same row/col, connect itself no fill. For any two same colored cells aligned, draws full segment.

Then weird boundary logic:
x24 height, x25 width.
x26 matcher(last, ZERO): location column j == 0? For an index tuple (i,j), last is j. x27 = width-1. x28 matcher(last, x27): j == w-1. x29 either => cell at left or right edge (j==0 or j==w-1).
x30 matcher(first, ZERO): i==0. x31 = h-1. x32 matcher(first,x31): i==h-1. x33 either => cell at top or bottom edge.
x34 = toindices(x4): indices of all non-background cells.

x36 = equality(x34, x35): True if all non-background cells are on left/right edges. i.e., no colored pixels in interior columns. (assuming colored pixels only at edges)

x39 = branch(x36, x29, x33). If all colored cells at left/right edge, use x29 (left/right edge predicate); else use x33 (top/bottom edge predicate).
x40 = asindices(I) all grid cells.
x41 = sfilter(x40, x39): all cells on either left/right edges (if condition true) or top/bottom edges (if false).
x42 = toobject(x41, I): object of those cells with their existing colors.
x43 = paint(x38, x42): paints edge cells into x38.
